title: A Promise of Light | Sri Daya Mata

# A Promise of Light: A Discourse by Sri Daya Mata

### Opening Reflections
Divine love is the greatest power in the universe. It is the very essence of God, and it is the bridge that connects the human soul to the Infinite. As I look into your faces, I do not see the superficial masks that the world wears. I see the souls behind the eyes—the sparks of the Divine waiting to be fanned into the roaring flame of realization.

We are all pilgrims on a journey back to our Source. Gurudeva, Paramahansa Yogananda, used to remind us constantly that we are not these bodies, nor these shifting emotions. We are the eternal Atman, the soul, which knows no birth and no death. When we center our consciousness in this truth, the problems of the world, no matter how heavy they may seem, begin to dissolve like mist before the rising sun.

### The Necessity of Personal Practice
Many people ask me, 'Daya Mataji, how can I find peace in such a turbulent time?' My answer is always the same: Go within. You cannot find lasting peace in the outside world, for the outside world is in a state of constant flux. It is the nature of Maya—the cosmic illusion—to change. If you build your happiness on the sands of worldly circumstances, it will be washed away by the tides of time.

### The Power of Introspection
**Story • The Traveler in the Fog**

Story: There was once a weary traveler who lost his way in a dense, dark forest during a heavy fog. He walked in circles for hours, growing more panicked, convinced that the path had disappeared entirely. He shouted for help, but only the hollow echo of his own voice returned. Finally, exhausted, he sat down beneath an old oak tree and closed his eyes. He realized that searching the darkness with his physical eyes was useless. He began to pray, turning his attention away from the confusing shapes in the forest and into the quiet center of his heart. As he surrendered his struggle, the fog did not vanish, but his perception shifted. He felt a guidance from within—a quiet, inner intuition. He stood up and followed that internal direction, not looking at the path, but looking toward the Light within. Shortly after, he emerged into a clear meadow, bathed in moonlight.

This is our condition. We are walking in the fog of our own desires, our own ego-attachments. We must sit beneath the tree of meditation and turn our gaze inward. When we do, the fog of delusion begins to lift.

### Devotion as the Path
Devotion is not merely a sentiment; it is a discipline. It is the heart's longing to return to the Father. When you sit in meditation, do not be satisfied with a mere mechanical practice. Pour your heart out. Let God know that you are hungry for His presence. If you come to Him with sincerity, He cannot hide. He is more eager to find you than you are to find Him.

### The Promise of Light
There is a promise that every saint has made throughout the ages: 'Ask, and it shall be given; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.' This is not a metaphor. It is a spiritual law as precise as the law of gravity. When you knock at the door of the Infinite through the techniques of Kriya Yoga and through the expansion of your own love, that door will swing open. You will find that you were never separated from Him in the first place.

May you live in that Light. May you carry that fragrance of the Divine into your homes, your workplaces, and your interactions with every soul you meet. You are never alone. The Guru’s love is a protective shield, and the Divine Mother’s embrace is always around you. Walk forward with courage, for the destination is already yours.
